# tests/fixtures/emergency-corpus.txt — command-shape corpus for the
# emergency-disclosure PreToolUse guard (issue #507).
#
# This file is DATA, not code. Each record is:
#
#   %%CASE <label>
#   %%HOME <repo-a|repo-b>      (optional; default repo-a's parent HOME)
#   ...command text, one or more lines...
#   %%END
#
# Placeholders substituted at load time:
#   %REPO_A%    a git repository (the hook cwd)
#   %REPO_B%    a second git repository whose path contains a space
#   %TEST_ROOT% the parent of both repositories
#
# Ground truth is NOT recorded here. tests/test-emergency-disclosure.sh runs
# every command under real Bash with a fake `git` on PATH that records
# protected pushes without contacting a remote, and that execution is the
# oracle. Recording expectations here would only pin one parser's opinion;
# the whole point of issue #507 is that the parser's opinion was wrong.
#
# Provenance:
#   - fixtures 1-90 are recovered from tests/test-emergency-parser-differential.sh
#     (deleted in 4bdaee0 "test: consolidate feature coverage"), which encoded
#     the review reproductions from PRs #492, #506, #665 and #725
#   - fixtures marked "current-suite" come from tests/test-emergency-disclosure.sh
#   - fixtures marked "issue" reproduce false positives reported on #507,
#     #634, #642, #646, #745 and #776
#   - fixtures marked "new" are hostile shapes added for this corpus

%%CASE compound-if-condition
%%EXPECT block
if git push --no-verify origin main; then printf ok; fi
%%END

%%CASE time-prefix
%%EXPECT block
time -p git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE command-substitution
%%EXPECT block
printf "%s" "$(git push --no-verify origin main)"
%%END

%%CASE shell-c-payload
%%EXPECT block
bash -c 'git push --no-verify origin main'
%%END

%%CASE invoked-function
%%EXPECT block
push_now() { git push --no-verify origin main; }; push_now
%%END

%%CASE sudo-wrapper
%%EXPECT block
sudo git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE nice-wrapper
%%EXPECT block
nice -n 5 git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE nohup-wrapper
%%EXPECT block
nohup git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE git-global-option
%%EXPECT block
git --no-pager push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE quoted-git-c
%%EXPECT block
git -C "%REPO_B%" push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE preceding-direct-cd
%%EXPECT block
cd "%REPO_B%" && git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE subshell-cd-before-outer-push
%%EXPECT block
(cd "%REPO_B%" && git status); git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE nested-substitution-cd
%%EXPECT block
printf '%s' $(cd "%REPO_B%" && git push --no-verify origin main)
%%END

%%CASE wrapped-shell-payload
%%EXPECT block
sudo bash -c 'git push --no-verify origin main'
%%END

%%CASE line-continuation
%%EXPECT block
git \
push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE apostrophe-in-double-quotes
%%EXPECT block
printf "%s" "it's $(git push --no-verify origin main)"
%%END

%%CASE nested-command-substitutions
%%EXPECT block
printf "%s" "$(printf "%s" "$(date)"; git push --no-verify origin main)"
%%END

%%CASE scoped-cd-before-outer-push
%%EXPECT block
(printf prep; cd "%REPO_B%"; printf done); git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE expanded-bypass-flag
%%EXPECT block
flag=--no-verify; git push "$flag" origin main
%%END

%%CASE command-local-cdpath
%%EXPECT block
CDPATH="%TEST_ROOT%"; cd "repo b" && git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE expanded-git-command
%%EXPECT block
cmd=git; "$cmd" push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE expanded-push-subcommand
%%EXPECT block
sub=push; git "$sub" --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE dynamic-git-environment
%%EXPECT block
"$GIT" push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE skipped-cd-before-push
%%EXPECT block
false && cd "%REPO_B%"; git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE literal-quoted-heredoc
%%EXPECT allow
cat >/dev/null <<'EOF'

%%END

%%CASE literal-unquoted-heredoc

$(git push --no-verify origin main)

%%END

(git push --no-verify origin main)
%%END

%%END

The split is safe — local scoping applies. Em dashes — twice.
EOF
)"
%%END

%%CASE new-backtick-push
%%EXPECT block
printf '%s' `git push --no-verify origin main`
%%END

%%EXPECT block
printf "%s" "`git push --no-verify origin main`"
%%END

printf '%s' "$(printf '%s' "$(git push --no-verify origin main)")"
%%END

%%CASE new-cd-parent-repo
%%EXPECT block
cd "%REPO_B%/.." && cd "repo b" && git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-function-forwards-args
%%EXPECT block
gp() { git push "$@"; }; gp --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-function-defined-then-called-later
%%EXPECT block
deploy() { git push --no-verify origin main; }
printf staging
deploy
%%END

%%CASE new-alias-then-invoke
%%EXPECT block
shopt -s expand_aliases
alias sync='git push --no-verify'
sync origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-heredoc-payload-into-bash
%%EXPECT block

git push --no-verify origin main

%%END

%%CASE new-heredoc-payload-into-sh-s

sh -s <<'EOF'
git push --no-verify origin main
EOF
%%END

%%CASE new-source-dev-stdin-heredoc
%%EXPECT block
source /dev/stdin <<'EOF'
git push --no-verify origin main
EOF
%%END

%%CASE new-here-string-into-bash
%%EXPECT block
bash -s <<<'git push --no-verify origin main'
%%END

%%CASE new-xargs-shell
%%EXPECT block
printf 'x\n' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'git push --no-verify origin main'
%%END

%%CASE new-find-exec-push
%%EXPECT block
find . -maxdepth 0 -exec git push --no-verify origin main \;
%%END

%%CASE new-eval-assembled-push
%%EXPECT block
part=push; eval "git $part --no-verify origin main"
%%END

%%CASE new-pipeline-tail-push
%%EXPECT block
printf 'x\n' | grep -q x && git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-multi-segment-semicolons
%%EXPECT block
printf one; printf two; printf three; git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-dynamic-brace-expansion-subcommand
%%EXPECT block
v=push; git ${v} --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-git-path-invocation
%%EXPECT block
/usr/bin/env git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-trailing-push-after-heredoc
%%EXPECT block
cat >/dev/null <<'EOF'
harmless prose
EOF
git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE new-tab-indented-heredoc-payload
%%EXPECT block
bash <<-EOF
	git push --no-verify origin main
EOF
%%END

# --- issue: false positives this work must fix ------------------------------

# The live false positive reported on #507 on 2026-08-12, verbatim in shape:
# three issue comments whose bodies are fed from quoted heredocs through a
# command substitution. No git, no push, no bypass flag is invoked anywhere.
# The guard it replaces refused this with
#   "multiple protected push segments require separate audited tool calls"
# because the heredoc consumer sat inside `$( … )`, which made its scanner
# treat the prose in the body as shell code.
%%CASE fp-issue-comment-batch-heredoc-substitution
%%EXPECT allow
gh issue comment 507 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
The hook refused this call saying it saw multiple protected push segments.
Nothing here invokes git push --no-verify; it is prose about the guard.
EOF
)"
gh issue comment 634 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Second finding: the same shape, describing git push --no-verify in prose.
EOF
)"
gh issue comment 745 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Third finding: also describing git push --no-verify in prose.
EOF
)"
%%END

%%CASE fp-issue-comment-batch-with-heredocs
%%EXPECT allow
cat > "%TEST_ROOT%/note-1.md" <<'EOF'
Blocked by the guard with "multiple protected push segments".
There was no git push in the command at all.
EOF
cat > "%TEST_ROOT%/note-2.md" <<'EOF'
The heredoc bodies were English prose describing findings.
Mentioning git push --no-verify in prose is not an invocation.
EOF
cat > "%TEST_ROOT%/note-3.md" <<'EOF'
Third note, same shape.
EOF
gh issue comment 507 --body-file "%TEST_ROOT%/note-1.md"
gh issue comment 634 --body-file "%TEST_ROOT%/note-2.md"
gh issue comment 745 --body-file "%TEST_ROOT%/note-3.md"
%%END

%%CASE fp-hostile-strings-as-quoted-data
%%EXPECT allow
printf '%s\n' 'git push --no-verify
cd /tmp && git push --no-verify
git -C /tmp push --no-verify'
%%END

%%CASE fp-hostile-strings-as-quoted-data-heredoc
%%EXPECT allow
cat >/dev/null <<'EOF'
git push --no-verify
cd /tmp && git push --no-verify
sudo git push --no-verify
EOF
%%END

%%CASE fp-multi-worktree-readonly-inventory
%%EXPECT allow
git status --short; git branch --show-current; git log -1 --oneline; git -C "%REPO_B%" status --short
%%END

%%CASE fp-cd-then-check-ignore
%%EXPECT allow
cd "%REPO_A%" && git check-ignore -v file.txt
%%END

%%CASE fp-cd-then-git-describe
%%EXPECT allow
cd "%REPO_A%" && git describe --tags --always
%%END

%%CASE fp-release-artifact-audit
%%EXPECT allow
gh release download v1.0.0 --pattern '*.dmg' --dir "%TEST_ROOT%" && printf verified
%%END

%%CASE fp-gh-issue-create-quoted-push-prose
%%EXPECT allow
gh issue create --title 'Guard blocks prose' --body 'The body describes git push --no-verify as prose, not as code.'
%%END

%%CASE fp-echo-prose-with-bypass-words
%%EXPECT allow
echo 'run git push --no-verify only in an emergency'
%%END

%%CASE fp-grep-pipeline-mentioning-push
%%EXPECT allow
printf 'git push --no-verify\n' | grep -c push
%%END

# The second reported false positive, verbatim in shape: hostile commands
# passed to this guard as test data, in one single-quoted argument that spans
# newlines. The guard it replaces split segments on newlines inside the quotes
# and refused with "multiple protected push segments", which meant the script
# could not be exercised from a shell without tripping over its own parser.
%%CASE fp-hostile-strings-single-quoted-multiline
%%EXPECT allow
printf '%s\n' 'git push --no-verify
cd /tmp && git push --no-verify
sudo git push --no-verify'
%%END

# --- deliberately conservative: refused although Bash executes no push ------
#
# These are NOT oracle-derived. Bash pushes nothing here because the variables
# are unset, but an argument or command word assembled at runtime could be the
# bypass flag or git itself. The guard being replaced refused both; recording
# them keeps a future simplification from quietly dropping the case.

%%CASE conservative-git-push-dynamic-argument
%%EXPECT block
git push origin "$branch"
%%END

%%CASE conservative-dynamic-command-word-with-bypass
%%EXPECT block
"$runner" push --no-verify origin main
%%END

# --- oversized input: the size-triggered fail-open class (issue #806) -------
#
# %FILLER% expands to 96 KiB, past the pipe buffer. A guard that tests its
# input with `producer | grep -q PATTERN` under `set -o pipefail` gets 141 on a
# MATCH at this size — grep exits on the first hit, the producer takes SIGPIPE,
# and pipefail surfaces the signal — so the match reads as a failure and the
# guard allows what it just recognized. Every other fixture in this corpus is
# small enough to finish writing before grep exits, which is exactly why the
# class was invisible. These must block for the same reason their small
# equivalents do.

%%CASE large-input-protected-push
%%EXPECT block
printf '%s' '%FILLER%'
git push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE large-input-heredoc-payload-into-bash
%%EXPECT block
bash <<'EOF'
%FILLER%
git push --no-verify origin main
EOF
%%END

%%CASE large-input-protected-push-in-substitution
%%EXPECT block
printf '%s' "$(printf '%s' '%FILLER%'; git push --no-verify origin main)"
%%END

%%CASE large-input-benign-prose
%%EXPECT allow
printf '%s' '%FILLER% git push --no-verify origin main'
%%END

# --- PR #810 review round 1: shapes the bounded guard allowed -----------------
#
# Every case below executes a protected push under real Bash and was blocked by
# the 2,021-line emulator this guard replaces. Each one was a regression against
# the no-weaker claim, not a pre-existing hole: the triage that produced them
# ran all fourteen against `git show origin/main:scripts/emergency-disclosure.sh`
# and that guard blocked all fourteen.

%%CASE git-alias-with-quoted-value
%%EXPECT block
git quoted-push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE config-include-contributes-alias
%%EXPECT block
git -c include.path=%TEST_ROOT%/include-alias.cfg included-push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE heredoc-into-shell-git-alias
%%EXPECT block
git shell-git <<'EOF'
git push --no-verify origin main
EOF
%%END

%%CASE env-split-string-payload
%%EXPECT block
env -S 'git push --no-verify origin main'
%%END

%%CASE text-producer-piped-to-interpreter
%%EXPECT block
printf 'git push --no-verify origin main' | bash
%%END

%%CASE arithmetic-expansion-nested-substitution
%%EXPECT block
echo $(( $(git push --no-verify origin main) + 1 ))
%%END

%%CASE arithmetic-command-nested-substitution
%%EXPECT block
(( total = $(git push --no-verify origin main) + 1 ))
%%END

%%CASE parameter-expansion-nested-substitution
%%EXPECT block
echo ${unset_fixture:-$(git push --no-verify origin main)}
%%END

%%CASE assigned-payload-through-eval
%%EXPECT block
cmd='git push --no-verify origin main'; eval "$cmd"
%%END

%%CASE assigned-payload-through-shell-c
%%EXPECT block
cmd='git push --no-verify origin main'; bash -c "$cmd"
%%END

%%CASE source-file-written-by-same-call
%%EXPECT block
printf '%s\n' 'git push --no-verify origin main' > %TEST_ROOT%/sourced-push.sh; source %TEST_ROOT%/sourced-push.sh
%%END

%%CASE foreign-interpreter-split-inputs
%%EXPECT block
awk -v a=git -v b='push --no-verify origin main' 'BEGIN { system(a " " b) }'
%%END

%%CASE dynamic-executable-through-env-wrapper
%%EXPECT block
GIT=git; env "$GIT" push --no-verify origin main
%%END

%%CASE dynamic-executable-through-sudo-wrapper
%%EXPECT block
GIT=git; sudo "$GIT" push --no-verify origin main
%%END
